title: Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR): an Address Assignment and Aggregation Strategy

claims_extracted.claim: CIDR was motivated by address-space pressure and explosive growth in routing tables.
claims_extracted.notes: Context for why classless interdomain routing became necessary.

claims_extracted.claim: CIDR requires routing destinations to be represented by arbitrary network-and-mask pairs rather than class A/B/C semantics, with longest-match forwarding semantics.
CIDR requires interdomain routing protocols to support route aggregation.
claims_extracted.notes: Connect to BGP-4 without treating CIDR as a feature invented solely inside BGP.

notes: Use alongside BGP-4 specifications to preserve the separate address-allocation/routing-scaling lineage that drove classless protocol changes.
